title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 187 (Investments of company to be held in its own name)

content.overview: Section 187 requires that all investments made or held by a company in any property, security or other asset shall be made and held by it in its own name: provided that the company may hold any shares in its subsidiary company in the name of any nominee or nominees of the company, if it is necessary to do so, to ensure that the number of members of the subsidiary company is not reduced below the statutory minimum. Further exceptions include investments held through a depository, and investments deposited with a bank or held in the name of a public official where required by law.
content.glance: Company investments must be held in the company’s own name; limited exceptions for nominee holding in a subsidiary (to meet statutory minimum members), depository holding, and bank/public-official holding where the law requires.
content.study: All investments made or held by a company in any property, security or other asset shall be made and held by it in its own name: Provided that the company may hold any shares in its subsidiary company in the name of any nominee or nominees of the company, if it is necessary to do so, to ensure that the number of members of the subsidiary company is not reduced below the statutory minimum. Nothing in this section shall be deemed to prevent a company from depositing with a bank, being the bankers of the company, any shares or securities for the collection of any dividend or interest payable thereon, or from depositing with, or transferring to, or holding in the name of, a depository any shares or securities. A register of investments not held in the company’s own name must be maintained where the section so requires. Beneficial ownership that is not disclosed may also engage sections 89 and 90. Current-law framing: confirm the investment is held in the company’s name; test whether a statutory exception applies; check register and beneficial-ownership disclosure if relevant.

sections.heading: Own-Name Rule
sections.body: Investments in property, security or other asset must be made and held in the company’s own name.

sections.heading: Subsidiary Nominee Exception
sections.body: Shares in a subsidiary may be held in the name of a nominee of the company where necessary to keep the subsidiary’s membership at or above the statutory minimum.

sections.heading: Depository and Bank Exceptions
sections.body: Holding through a depository, or depositing with the company’s bankers for collection of dividend/interest, is permitted.

sections.heading: Register and Beneficial Ownership
sections.body: Where investments are not held in the company’s own name under an exception, the prescribed register is maintained; ss. 89 and 90 may also apply to beneficial ownership.

provisions.title: Investments of company to be held in its own name

examples.title: Nominee for subsidiary membership
examples.body: A holding company holds one share of its wholly owned subsidiary in the name of a nominee solely to meet the statutory minimum number of members. Section 187 permits that limited nominee holding.

examples.title: Investment in director’s name
examples.body: A company holds listed equity in the personal name of a director without a statutory exception. Section 187 is breached; the investment should be in the company’s own name.

hypotheticals.question: May a company hold all its investments through a director as nominee for convenience?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The general rule is that investments must be held in the company’s own name. Nominee holding is allowed only in the narrow cases the section states (e.g. subsidiary minimum membership), not for general convenience.

distinctions.title: Investments in own name (s. 187) vs inter-corporate loans/investments (s. 186)
distinctions.left: How title to investments is held
distinctions.right: Quantitative ceilings and approvals for inter-corporate deployment

misconceptions.trap: Nominee holding of company investments is freely allowed.
misconceptions.correction: Nominee holding is exceptional and limited (e.g. subsidiary membership minimum). The default is holding in the company’s own name.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 187 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm investment is held in company’s name. II. Test statutory exception. III. Check register/beneficial-ownership rules. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Holding facts; exception if any; register status; precise relief.

examTips: Default: hold in company’s own name.
Narrow nominee exception for subsidiary membership.
